h1: The 8 Best Robot Vacuums Without Subscriptions of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best No-Fee Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 robot vacuums that need no paid plan, scored on free app features, upkeep costs and floors, from roborock to Shark and eufy.
summary: The roborock Q7 M5+ is the best overall, with 10,000Pa suction, mopping and a dock rated up to 7 to 9 weeks, plus free mapping. The Shark AV2501S is the pet-hair pick with a bagless base, the roborock Q10 S5+ matches the suction, and the Shark Navigator is a plain docked vacuum. The eufy 11S MAX, ILIFE A30s, Lefant M210 and Tikom G8000 Max cover budgets.
intro: Subscription creep has reached robot vacuums. Some makers now fence off mapping, no-go zones or cleaning history behind a monthly fee, so a robot that looks like a bargain at checkout can start nudging you toward a plan within a year. Because the paywall sits in the app, the box and the product photos never mention it.

The robots here keep their useful features free. Our editors reviewed eight whose core functions, such as scheduling and room mapping, run without a paid tier, and ranked them on suction, dock design, navigation and recurring costs. Dock bags and replacement parts count as running costs, since a free app that sends you to buy bags every month is not truly free, and cheap robots can hide costly parts.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: 10,000Pa, mopping and a dock rated up to 7 to 9 weeks. Mapping and scheduling stay free.
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ pairs 10,000Pa of suction with a mop and a self-empty base rated to run up to 7 to 9 weeks before you swap the bag. Mapping, room scheduling and no-go zones all run in the app without a paid tier. Suction in Pascals indicates how hard the motor pulls dirt out of carpet fibres.

It ranks first because it keeps both costs and chores low: the dock interval means few bag swaps, and the app features stay free. The Shark has no bags to buy at all, but it lacks a mop and its dock holds only about a month.

Buy it for mixed floors and a hands-off routine. The caveats: it is not the cheapest here, in the $200 to $500 bucket, and dock bags are a small ongoing cost.
cons: Dock bags are a small ongoing cost
products.idealFor: Mixed-floor homes that want weeks of hands-off cleaning.
products.skipIf: You want the lowest possible purchase price.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Self-Empty Base
products.verdict: Bagless HEPA base with about 30 days of capacity. No bags to buy, ever.
products.description:
Shark's Matrix Clean navigation and home mapping drive the AV2501S, and its base is bagless, holding dirt in a HEPA-filtered bin good for roughly 30 days. Skipping bags removes the one recurring cost most self-empty docks have, and HEPA filtering keeps fine dust from leaking back when you empty the bin.

It lands second because the roborock offers a longer interval and a mop. For pet owners who dislike buying bags, though, the Shark's running cost is as low as it gets in a docked robot.

Buy it for a pet household with hard floors and carpet. Skip it if you want mopping. The caveat is the shorter interval: about 30 days against 7 to 9 weeks, so a heavy-shedding home will empty the bin more often. Free app scheduling is included.
products.idealFor: Pet households that dislike buying bags.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.verdict: Another 10,000Pa roborock with its own self-empty base. Free core features.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ matches the Q7 M5+ on 10,000Pa suction in a different combo configuration with its own self-empty base. Cleaning, mapping and scheduling work without a subscription, as with the rest of roborock's Q-series. It vacuums and mops.

It ranks below the Q7 because the Q7 states a longer dock interval, which is the clearer advantage, while this listing does not. The two share so much that your choice may come down to price on the day.

Buy it if you want strong suction and a self-empty dock from a brand that keeps its app free. Skip it if you care most about the longest dock interval. The caveat: the overlap with the Q7 means you gain nothing new, so compare the current prices of both before you commit.
products.idealFor: Roborock fans wanting strong suction at a similar level.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum with Self-Empty Base
products.verdict: A vacuum-only Shark with a self-empty base and app scheduling at a lower feature tier.
products.description:
The Navigator brings a self-empty base to Shark's lineup at a lower tier than the AI Ultra, with standard navigation and app scheduling. It does not mop, and nothing it offers needs a subscription. A self-empty base cuts hand emptying down to weeks.

Because it skips the Matrix Clean navigation of the AI Ultra, expect plainer cleaning paths and no true room mapping. In return, you get the dock convenience for less money, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Buy it for a small to mid-sized home that wants an inexpensive docked vacuum. Skip it if you want mapping or mopping. The caveat: standard navigation covers a floor less efficiently, so large layouts take longer and may leave patches, which the AI Ultra and roborock models avoid.
products.idealFor: Small to mid-sized homes wanting an inexpensive docked vacuum.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner
products.verdict: Super thin and quiet, with no dock and no bags. Fits under low furniture.
products.description:
The 11S MAX is slim enough to slip beneath low furniture that blocks taller robots, and it is quieter than the high-suction combos. With no dock there are no bags to buy, only a dust bin to empty by hand. App and remote control are included, and it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

It skips mopping and advanced room mapping, which is why it ranks fifth. The compromise is clear: fewer features for a lower running cost.

Choose it for an apartment with low sofas and a need for quiet. Skip it if you want a self-empty dock or a mop. The caveat is the manual emptying, which you will do after most runs, and lower suction than the 10,000Pa picks on thick carpet.
products.idealFor: Apartments with low furniture and quiet needs.
products.skipIf: You want a self-empty dock or mop.

products.name: ILIFE A30s Robot Vacuum
products.verdict: 10,000Pa max suction at roughly half the price of combos, with basic free app control.
products.description:
The A30s lists 10,000Pa max suction, the same headline as pricier combo units, at about half their price. Scheduling and self-charging run through the app with no subscription needed. A max suction figure refers to the highest setting, so expect more noise there.

At this price there is no self-empty dock and no true mapping, which is why it ranks sixth. If you only need a robot to run on a schedule over simple floors, those omissions cost you little.

Buy it for strong suction on a budget. Skip it if you need mapping or docked emptying. The caveat: a 10,000Pa headline in a budget unit is the maker's maximum rating, so compare real owner feedback on carpet before relying on it for deep cleaning.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want strong suction.
products.skipIf: You need mapping or docked emptying.

products.name: Lefant Robot Vacuum Cleaner M210
products.verdict: 120 minutes of runtime, Alexa control and a slim, low-noise body. No account fee.
products.description:
The M210 is a small vacuum that runs for 120 minutes, accepts Wi-Fi and Alexa commands and returns to charge by itself. Daily scheduling needs no paid account. Its slim, low-noise body suits small flats and studios.

There is no self-empty base, so upkeep is emptying the bin and cleaning brushes and filters. It is a budget model with modest suction, which puts it below the others, and it costs $50 to $100.

Buy it for a studio with simple floors and a limited budget. Skip it if you need strong carpet suction. The caveat: with modest suction, the M210 is best on hard floors and low-pile rugs, and its 120 minute runtime is plenty for a small space but not a large home.
products.idealFor: Small flats and studios with simple floors.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo G8000 Max
products.verdict: A budget vacuum and mop combo with a physical remote and 150 minutes of runtime.
products.description:
The G8000 Max combines vacuuming and mopping with 5000Pa suction, a 150 minute runtime and both app and physical remote control. Nothing about scheduling or the mop function needs a subscription. The remote means you can start it without a phone.

Suction is the lowest in the guide, which is why it ranks last. The remote is a useful touch for anyone who does not want to depend on an app, and the runtime is the longest in the guide.

Buy it for light cleaning on mixed hard floors. Skip it if you have thick carpet or heavy pet hair. The caveat: there is no self-empty dock, and 5000Pa is half the figure of the roborock and ILIFE models, so it will leave debris in carpet that a stronger robot would lift.
products.idealFor: Light cleaning on mixed hard floors.
products.skipIf: You have thick carpet or heavy pet hair.

whatMatters.detail: Mapping, room cleaning, no-go zones and cleaning history are the features most often locked behind paid tiers. Read the listing and the maker's app description for any mention of a premium plan. If you cannot find clear wording, assume that feature may be gated, and ask before you buy a robot from a brand you do not know.

Bagged docks use disposable bags that cost a few dollars each. A bagless base like the Shark AV2501S has none, but you empty a bin about monthly. Pet households fill bags faster, so check the bag size and the spare price. Count the cost over two years, not just the purchase day.

A self-empty dock cuts hand emptying to weeks apart. Without one, you empty the bin after most runs. Check the listing for a base included, not sold separately, since several brands sell the dock as an add-on. The Shark Navigator and roborock models include theirs, while the 11S MAX, A30s and M210 have none.

Mapped navigation plans rows and remembers rooms. Basic navigation bounces around and may miss areas. If you want room-specific cleaning, look for mapping in the spec bullets. The roborock models and the AI Ultra list mapping, while the Navigator, 11S MAX and M210 do not. Mapping is where subscriptions hide, so check it.

Measure the gap under your sofa and bed. Slim robots like the eufy 11S MAX fit under low furniture, while taller models with a laser turret can get stuck. Compare the robot height with your clearance, and remember that a stuck robot is a robot you rescue every week. The listing may show height in the specifications.

faq.q: Do robot vacuums really charge subscriptions?
faq.a: A few do, charging monthly for mapping, no-go zones or cleaning history. Every robot here keeps those core features free, but app terms change, so read the maker's app description for a premium tier before you order.

faq.q: Is the roborock Q7 M5+ worth it over the ILIFE A30s?
faq.a: If you want a dock, a mop and a saved map, yes. The ILIFE A30s lists the same 10,000Pa headline for less, but it has no self-empty base and no true mapping, so you do more by hand.

faq.q: Do I need a self-empty base?
faq.a: Not in a small flat, where emptying a bin every few runs takes seconds. In a larger or pet-heavy home, a dock such as the Shark Navigator's saves frequent trips and keeps dust out of the air.

faq.q: What are the hidden costs of a robot vacuum?
faq.a: Replacement brushes, filters, mop pads and dock bags add up. Bagged docks like roborock's cost a few dollars per bag, while a bagless Shark base avoids that expense but needs its bin emptied about monthly.

faq.q: Can a robot vacuum work without Wi-Fi?
faq.a: On a basic level, yes. Models with a physical remote or buttons, like the Tikom G8000 Max, run without a phone. Mapping and scheduling usually need the app, which in turn needs a network connection.

faq.q: Will a slim robot like the eufy 11S MAX clean carpets?
faq.a: It copes with light carpet but is built for hard floors and tight gaps. For thick pile and pet hair, a higher-suction model such as the roborock or Shark does a better job and empties itself.

finalTake: Buy the Q7 M5+ for mixed floors and weeks of hands-off cleaning, or the Shark AV2501S if pets mean bags would pile up. Choose the Navigator for a cheap dock, the 11S MAX for low furniture, and the ILIFE, Lefant or Tikom only when budget outweighs suction. Check the maker's app description for premium tiers.
